How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Chair’ s
discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the Community Services
Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the Commission
before the meeting for their consideration but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted
after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

   MINUTES OF APRIL 7, 2025
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Duong called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at 6:34
P.M. on Monday, April 7, 2025, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at City
Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Lotz.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Nancy Duong, Davis Barrantes, Justin Lotz and Darwin
  Rodriguez

Youth Ambassadors Present:  Angie Phan and Carly Zhao.

Commissioners Absent:  None.

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Assistant Director Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit
comments and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services
Commission, email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  APRIL 7, 2025
   Public Comment by George Young.

  He provided some history regarding the San Gabriel Sea Gulls. Their program is nearing 35
  years and they just completed their fall/winter season in March. He wanted to introduce
  himself and would like to attend more meetings. He thanks the commission for being here
  and supporting the city.

3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Barrantes, seconded by Commissioner Lotz to
  approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for March 3,
  2025.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0 as follows:

  AYES:  BARRANTES, DUONG, LOTZ, RODRIGUEZ
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. PRESENTATION OF OUTREACH EFFORTS PERFORMED BY THE CITY PUBLIC
  INFORMATION OFFICER
  Presented by Public Information Officer Flores.

  The Commission thanked the PIO for her presentation, they had questions regarding
  LinkedIn, WeChat and other multi-ethnic applications. They would like to make sure
  that the city is trying to reach residents where English is not their primary language.
  They also asked about awareness and safety near schools and drivers who do not stop
  when buses are stopped, and their lights are flashing.

  They wondered if the city would utilize TIKTOK and engage the youth to assist.

  The commission shared they would like to create a survey to find out the demographic
  of the public attending our events.

  Public Comment: None

  B. SPRING SWIM REGISTRATION RECAP AND SUMMER REGISTRATION
  UPDATE
  Presented by Supervisor Shoup

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  APRIL 7, 2025
   The Commission thanked Supervisor Shoup for the update. They asked how the
  department would gather contacts and information regarding adaptive learning
  classes. They asked if there would be issues with staffing and if classes would be
  expanding in the future.

  C. DISCUSSION ON POSSIBLE PROGRAMMING FOR NEURODIVERGENT
  RESIDENTS
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens

  The Commission submitted information to the department recently. They shared
  information regarding programs. The Commission is thinking of creating a Facebook
  group to collect contacts. They also discussed trying to gain funding for programming.
  They would like to see how the city of Duarte puts their event together.

  The Commission asked if there were facilities available that lend themselves to sensory
  sensitivity activities.

  Public Comment: None

  D. EVENTS AND PROGRAMS UPDATES
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens

  The Commission asked for signage at the park regarding the construction/closure of
  the parking lot. They had questions regarding the upcoming Art Exhibition and if the
  artists are from San Gabriel or other cities.

  E. DISCUSSION OF WORKPLAN
  Presented by Chair Duong

  They felt the PIO’s presentation provided a lot of information regarding their desires
  to reach various demographics. They discussed how they can obtain information
  regarding targeting diverse audiences. They will revamp the workplan at the next
  meeting.

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS
  Commissioner Lotz hopes that things work out with the inclusive playground.

  Youth Ambassadors Phan and Zhao believe everything is going well.

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  None.

7. ADJOURNMENT

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  APRIL 7, 2025

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  December 2, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2024 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting. The draft for 2024 outlined in this report
includes items from the 2023 workplan and the amendments made at the November 6,
2023 and February 5, 2024 commission meetings. The Community Services Commission
approved the workplan at the March 4, 2024 commission meeting. At the October 7, 2024
commission meeting the Community Services Commission decided to change it from an
annual workplan to an ongoing document that can be adjusted if and when needed to
better address the needs of the department. The Commission will conduct a
comprehensive evaluation of the workplan every six months to determine if major
changes need to be made.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.
 Purpose of the Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.

Current Workplan
The workplan sets four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore. The list below reflects amendments made at the November 4,
2024 Community Services Commission Meeting.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Provide new programs for residents with the age groups, 13-18 and 30-50.
  b. Explore program offerings for persons with disabilities including but not
  limited to swim classes.

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.

Next Steps:
  1. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  a. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
  2. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  a. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information.

Completed Tasks:
  1. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to assist
  in the development and implementation of events and services.
  a. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native American
  Community and interfaith groups
  2. Recommend that City Council approve the release of an RFP for a new
  registration software during fiscal year 2024/25.
 3. Recommend that City Council approve the addition of a part time case manager
  through a third party provider.
4. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
5. Commission to develop a youth ambassador program, host interviews and appoint
  two non-voting ambassadors to the commission.
